Cable spent decades charging you for 200 channels to watch a handful of games each week. That era is over — but the replacement isn't as simple as canceling and moving on. [Cheaper options](https://www.engadget.com/2246400/cheapest-nfl-streaming-options-stay-locked-in-all-season/) genuinely exist for every fan type, and a **one-time antenna purchase** alone gets you local CBS, FOX, NBC, and ABC games at zero recurring cost. The honest tradeoff: going cheap means more apps, more switching, and more managed inconvenience. Know that going in.

## Free First: Why an Antenna Is Still Your Best Opening Move

_A modest piece of hardware remains the shrewdest first move any budget-conscious NFL fan can make._

Advertisement

Advertisement

Advertisement

According to comparesubscriptions.com, an [over-the-air antenna is the lowest-cost](https://comparesubscriptions.com/live-tv/best-way-to-watch-nfl-2026) foundation for NFL Sundays — local network games, no monthly bill, no login required. Stack that against a full live-TV bundle running **$70-plus per month**, and the antenna pays for itself well before Week 1 ends.

## Build Your Stack by Fan Type

_What you actually need depends entirely on which kind of fan you are._

What you actually need depends on your viewing habits:

*   **Local-team fan:** antenna only, or add [NFL+ at $6.99/month](https://support.nfl.com/hc/en-us/articles/35869739723028-How-much-does-NFL-cost) ($49.99/season) if you need mobile streaming, per the NFL's official support page
    
*   **Primetime fan:** antenna plus [Prime Video ($14.99/month](https://theyearlybill.com/prices/amazon-prime/) or $139/year) for Thursday Night Football, plus [Peacock Premium ($10.99/month)](https://sports.yahoo.com/articles/watch-every-2026-nfl-game
